name: Risk Department
description: Organisational department responsible for credit risk assessment and management, including mortgage underwriting guidance and risk appetite oversight. Listed as owner and responsible party for this credit risk assessment guide.
ownership: Credit risk assessment and mortgage underwriting governance
accountability_finding: Responsible for credit risk policy, assessment methodology, and underwriting standards

name: Lending Department
description: Organisational department responsible for mortgage lending operations and underwriting execution. Shares ownership of the credit risk assessment guide with the Risk department.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team
ownership: Mortgage product delivery and underwriting execution
accountability_finding: Responsible for implementing credit risk assessment procedures in mortgage underwriting

name: Mortgage Product
description: Residential mortgage lending product subject to credit risk assessment and underwriting controls. This guide provides the framework for mortgage underwriting at FirstUK Bank.
context: FirstUK Bank — Credit Risk Assessment Guide (Mortgage Underwriting)
Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team

name: Mortgage Underwriter
description: Bank staff responsible for executing mortgage credit risk assessment and underwriting decisions in accordance with this guide. Primary audience for the credit risk assessment framework.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team
accountability: Execute credit risk assessment and underwriting decisions on mortgage applications

name: Risk Analyst
description: Bank staff responsible for analysing credit risk and supporting underwriting decisions. Audience for the credit risk assessment guide.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team
accountability: Support credit risk assessment methodology and monitoring

name: Head of Risk
description: Senior leadership role responsible for ownership and governance of the credit risk assessment guide. Accountable for risk framework oversight and policy maintenance.
accountability: Owner of Credit Risk Assessment Guide and overall credit risk governance

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk associated with residential mortgage lending, managed within FirstUK Bank's defined risk appetite of less than 0.5% loss ratio. This risk category governs the assessment and approval of mortgage applications to ensure consistent lending decisions.
context: Provide standardized procedures for assessing credit risk on residential mortgage applications
ensuring consistent lending decisions aligned with FirstUK Bank's risk appetite (<0.5% loss ratio)
appetite_rationale: Standardized procedures for residential mortgage lending require tight control to maintain portfolio quality

name: Mortgage Loss Ratio
description: Quantitative risk appetite threshold for residential mortgage portfolio, expressed as a maximum acceptable loss ratio. FirstUK Bank's stated appetite is less than 0.5%.
context: FirstUK Bank's risk appetite (<0.5% loss ratio)

name: Mortgage Credit Risk
description: FirstUK Bank's defined credit risk category for mortgage portfolios, with stated appetite thresholds for loss ratios, default rates, and borrower leverage constraints. The risk framework establishes maximum acceptable loss at 0.5% annually and default rate tolerance at <2% of active mortgages.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target
Maximum Loss Ratio: 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)
Default Rate Target: <2% (max 2% of active mortgages in default at any time)
LTV Limit: Max 95% (no negative equity scenarios)
stated_prohibitions: No negative equity scenarios

name: Maximum Loss Ratio
description: Quantitative risk appetite threshold for FirstUK Bank's mortgage portfolio, expressed as a maximum annual loss ratio of 0.5%, equivalent to £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio.
context: Maximum Loss Ratio: 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)

name: Default Rate Target
description: Key risk indicator for mortgage portfolio health, with a target threshold of <2%, representing the maximum acceptable proportion of active mortgages in default at any time.
context: Default Rate Target: <2% (max 2% of active mortgages in default at any time)

name: Loan-to-Value Limit
description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio constraint of 95% applied to mortgage origination, designed to prevent negative equity scenarios and protect against property value depreciation.
context: LTV Limit: Max 95% (no negative equity scenarios)

name: Debt-to-Income Limit
description: Maximum debt-to-income ratio of 45% applied as a borrower income constraint during mortgage underwriting, to ensure borrower repayment capacity.

name: Mortgage
description: FirstUK Bank's mortgage product subject to defined credit risk appetite, loss ratio targets, default rate thresholds, and borrower leverage constraints outlined in the credit risk framework.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target

name: Loss Ratio
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring credit losses as a percentage of portfolio value. The target threshold is set at less than 0.5%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 0.23%, indicating performance well within risk appetite.

name: Default Rate
description: A key risk indicator tracking the percentage of accounts in default status. The target threshold is less than 2%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 1.2%, demonstrating strong credit quality within risk appetite.

name: Average Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: A risk metric measuring the average loan-to-value ratio across the mortgage or secured lending portfolio. The target threshold is less than 80%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 72%, indicating conservative lending practices.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: A risk metric measuring the average debt-to-income ratio of borrowers in the portfolio. The target threshold is less than 45%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 38%, reflecting conservative underwriting standards.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A mortgage lending product subject to underwriting assessment. The document outlines the application assessment process for mortgage products, including evaluation of borrower information, property details, and loan terms.

name: Borrower
description: A natural person applying for a mortgage product. The underwriting process captures borrower information including personal details, employment, income, credit history, assets, and liabilities for assessment.

name: Mortgage Account
description: A mortgage account established following underwriting assessment. The account is defined by loan term, rate type (fixed or variable), and property collateral.

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk associated with mortgage lending, assessed through borrower credit history, CIBIL score, past defaults, income stability, and existing liabilities. This risk is evaluated as part of the mortgage application assessment process.

name: Property Valuation Risk
description: Risk related to the adequacy and stability of property collateral securing the mortgage. Assessment includes professional property valuation, property type, location, and area risk assessment.

name: Payment History Risk
description: Credit risk factor assessing borrower payment behaviour, weighted at 35% in the automated credit scoring model. Ranges from no missed payments (excellent) to regular late payments (poor), directly influencing credit score and lending decision.
context: Payment History | 35% | No missed payments (excellent) → Regular late payments (poor)
appetite_rationale: Payment history is the largest factor (35% weight) in credit scoring; missed or late payments indicate borrower default risk
controls_in_place: Automated credit score assessment
Payment history tracking as 35% weighting factor
stated_prohibitions: Regular late payments result in poor credit assessment

name: Credit Utilization Risk
description: Credit risk factor measuring the proportion of available credit used by the borrower, weighted at 20% in the scoring model. Low card balances indicate good credit management, while high balances signal elevated risk.
context: Credit Utilization | 20% | Low balance on cards (good) → High balance (poor)
appetite_rationale: High credit card balances relative to limits indicate elevated financial stress and default risk
controls_in_place: Credit utilization monitoring as 20% weighting factor in automated scoring
stated_prohibitions: High balance on cards results in poor credit assessment

name: Credit Age Risk
description: Credit risk factor reflecting the length of the borrower's credit history, weighted at 15% in the scoring model. Longer credit history demonstrates established creditworthiness, while new credit only indicates higher risk.
context: Credit Age | 15% | Longer credit history (good) → New credit only (poor)
appetite_rationale: Longer credit history demonstrates established borrowing behavior; new credit only indicates limited track record
controls_in_place: Credit age assessment as 15% weighting factor in automated scoring

name: Credit Inquiry Risk
description: Credit risk factor assessing the frequency of recent credit inquiries, weighted at 10% in the scoring model. Few recent inquiries indicate stable credit-seeking behaviour, while many recent inquiries suggest financial distress or over-leveraging.
context: Credit Inquiries | 10% | Few recent inquiries (good) → Many recent inquiries (poor)
appetite_rationale: Multiple recent credit inquiries may signal financial distress or aggressive credit-seeking behavior
controls_in_place: Credit inquiry monitoring as 10% weighting factor in automated scoring
stated_prohibitions: Many recent inquiries result in poor credit assessment

name: Default and Delinquency Risk
description: Credit risk factor measuring the borrower's history of defaults or delinquencies, weighted at 20% in the automated credit scoring model. No defaults indicate excellent credit standing, while recent defaults signal very high risk.
appetite_rationale: Recent defaults or delinquencies are strong indicators of imminent default risk on new credit
controls_in_place: Default and delinquency history assessment as 20% weighting factor in automated scoring
stated_prohibitions: Recent defaults result in very high risk classification

name: Automated Credit Score
description: Quantitative credit scoring metric on a 0–100 scale used to assess borrower creditworthiness and determine lending decisions. Score ranges from Very Poor (<60) to Excellent (90–100), with corresponding risk ratings and automated or manual underwriting actions.
context: 90–100 | Excellent | Very Low | Auto-Approve (if other criteria met)

name: Excellent Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating excellent creditworthiness with very low risk, triggering automatic approval if other lending criteria are met. Represents the bank's appetite for lowest-risk borrowers.
context: 90–100 | Excellent | Very Low | Auto-Approve (if other criteria met)

name: Good Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating good creditworthiness with low risk, requiring standard underwriting procedures. Represents the bank's appetite for low-risk borrowers with routine review.

name: Fair Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating fair creditworthiness with medium risk, requiring enhanced review procedures. Represents the bank's tolerance for medium-risk borrowers with additional scrutiny.

name: Poor Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating poor creditworthiness with high risk, requiring manager review and potential decline. Represents the bank's lower tolerance for high-risk borrowers.

name: Very Poor Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating very poor creditworthiness with very high risk, resulting in automatic decline. Represents the bank's minimum acceptable credit quality threshold.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A mortgage lending product subject to income qualification and verification procedures. The document establishes underwriting criteria for primary and secondary income assessment, including employment history verification, income stability evaluation, and conservative qualification factors applied to different employment and income types.
context: Primary Income (Employment): Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)

name: Income Verification Process
description: A Know Your Customer control requiring verification of applicant income through employer letters, employment history checks, and assessment of income stability. The process applies differentiated qualification factors based on employment type and income source to calculate conservative qualifying income.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)
Assess income stability (stable job vs. new employment)
consequence_of_failure: income cannot be qualified for mortgage calculation

name: Mortgage Applicant
description: A prospective customer applying for a mortgage product, subject to income verification and qualification procedures. The applicant's income is assessed across primary employment and secondary income sources using defined qualification factors.
context: Spouse income: Only if married/civil partnership
eligibility_or_verification_status: subject to income verification and employment stability assessment

name: Employer
description: The applicant's employer, whose verification is required as part of income assessment. Employment letters on company letterhead are used to confirm employment status, tenure, and income.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)
accountability: provide employment verification letter on company letterhead

name: Employment Stability Risk
description: A credit risk factor reflecting the applicant's employment tenure and type. The risk is mitigated through differentiated qualification factors: permanent employment of 2+ years qualifies at 100%, while permanent employment under 2 years qualifies at 75%, and self-employment under 2 years is not acceptable.
context: Assess income stability (stable job vs. new employment)
appetite_rationale: employment tenure directly impacts income sustainability for mortgage repayment
stated_prohibitions: self-employed applicants with less than 2 years trading history not acceptable
controls_in_place: minimum 2 years employment history requirement
differentiated qualification factors by employment type
employer verification via letterhead
tolerance_thresholds: contract employment >1 year remaining: 75% income qualification

name: Secondary Income Volatility Risk
description: A credit risk reflecting the variability and sustainability of secondary income sources. The risk is managed through conservative qualification factors: bonus and commission income qualifies at 50% of average, rental income at 75% to account for vacancy, and dividend/pension income at 100% if sustainable and stable.
appetite_rationale: secondary income sources are less stable and require conservative qualification
controls_in_place: reduced qualification factors for variable income
minimum history requirements for secondary income sources
tolerance_thresholds: dividend income: 100% if sustainable and >2 years history

name: Income Documentation Risk
description: A compliance risk related to the authenticity and sufficiency of income documentation. The risk is controlled through requirements for employer letters on company letterhead and minimum 2-year employment history verification.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)
appetite_rationale: inadequate documentation creates fraud and misrepresentation risk
controls_in_place: employer verification requirement
tax return review for self-employed
dividend statement verification
pension documentation review

name: Spouse Income Dependency Risk
description: A credit risk arising from reliance on spouse income in qualifying income calculations. The risk is controlled by limiting spouse income qualification to documented married or civil partnership status only.
context: Spouse income: Only if married/civil partnership
stated_prohibitions: spouse income only acceptable if applicant is married or in civil partnership
controls_in_place: marital status verification requirement
spouse income subject to same qualification factors as primary applicant

name: Permanent Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from permanent employment of 2 or more years. This metric represents the bank's appetite to accept full stated salary as qualifying income for stable, long-tenure employment.

name: New Permanent Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from permanent employment of less than 2 years. This metric reflects reduced appetite for income stability in newer employment, qualifying at 75% of stated salary.

name: Contract Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from contract employment with more than 1 year remaining. This metric qualifies contract income at 75% of stated salary, reflecting uncertainty in contract renewal.
context: Contract, >1 year remaining: 75% of stated salary
metric_name: Contract Employment >1 Year Remaining Qualification Factor

name: Self-Employed Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from self-employment of 2 or more years. This metric qualifies self-employed income at 75% of average last 2 years, reflecting income volatility and documentation complexity.
context: Self-employed, 2+ years: 75% of average last 2 years

name: Bonus and Commission Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to bonus and commission income. This metric qualifies such income at 50% of average last 2 years, reflecting significant volatility and discretionary nature.

name: Rental Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary rental income. This metric qualifies rental income at 75%, with the 25% reduction accounting for potential vacancy periods and maintenance costs.

name: Dividend Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary dividend income when sustainable and supported by 2+ years history. This metric qualifies dividend income at 100%, reflecting confidence in sustained investment returns.
period: sustainable dividend income with >2 years history

name: Pension and Benefits Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary pension and benefits income when guaranteed and stable. This metric qualifies such income at 100%, reflecting the certainty of government-backed or contractually guaranteed payments.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A residential mortgage product with a principal amount of £300,000, offered at 4.5% interest rate over a 25-year term. The product is subject to debt assessment and affordability evaluation as part of the lending decision process.

name: Car Loan
description: A car financing product included in the debt assessment calculation. Monthly payments are factored into the applicant's total debt obligations.

name: Credit Card Product
description: A credit card product included in debt assessment. Outstanding balances are calculated at 5% of the balance or the minimum payment, whichever is higher, for affordability purposes.
context: Credit Cards | Yes (5% of balance, or minimum payment, whichever higher)
debt_assessment_inclusion: 5% of balance or minimum payment, whichever higher

name: Student Loan
description: A student financing product included in the debt assessment. Actual monthly payments are included in the total debt obligations calculation.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: A key affordability metric calculated as total monthly debt obligations (including proposed mortgage) divided by gross monthly income. Used to assess lending risk and borrower capacity to service debt.
context: Debt-to-Income Ratio = (Monthly Debt + Mortgage) / Monthly Income
calculation_basis: (total monthly debt obligations + proposed mortgage payment) / gross monthly income

name: Proposed Mortgage Payment Calculation
description: The calculated monthly mortgage payment obligation of £1,519 derived from a £300,000 principal at 4.5% interest over 300 months. This payment is included in the debt-to-income ratio assessment.
monitoring_or_reporting_obligation: debt-to-income ratio calculation for lending decision

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Credit risk assessment based on the ratio of mortgage amount to property value. FirstUK Bank applies differentiated LTV limits by credit grade, with risk escalating from low risk at ≤70% LTV to very high risk at >95% LTV. Higher LTV ratios indicate reduced equity buffers and increased default probability.
context: FirstUK Bank LTV Limits by Credit Grade

description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with excellent credit grade (90+). FirstUK Bank permits up to 95% LTV for this segment at standard pricing with no rate premium applied.

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Good Credit Grade

canonical_name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Poor Credit Grade

description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with poor credit grade (60–69). FirstUK Bank permits up to 80% LTV for this segment; applications may be declined at higher LTV ratios.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Very Poor Credit Grade
canonical_name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Very Poor Credit Grade

description: Lending policy for customers with very poor credit grade (<60). FirstUK Bank does not offer mortgage lending to this segment; all applications are declined regardless of LTV.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: Mortgage Product
description: FirstUK Bank's mortgage lending product subject to LTV-based credit risk assessment and pricing differentiation by credit grade. The product applies tiered LTV limits and rate premiums based on borrower credit quality and equity position.
context: FirstUK Bank LTV Limits by Credit Grade

name: Property Location Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating property location stability and market conditions. Ranges from prime areas with stable values (low risk) through growing suburban areas (medium risk) to declining areas (high risk). Location directly impacts property value sustainability and collateral quality.
context: Location | Prime area, stable values | Growing suburban | Declining area
appetite_rationale: Location stability directly impacts property value and collateral quality
stated_prohibitions: Declining areas classified as high risk
controls_in_place: Location classification framework (prime, suburban, declining)
Market stability assessment

name: Property Type Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the property type and construction characteristics. Standard property types (houses, flats) present low risk, newer construction presents medium risk, and unusual properties such as listed buildings present high risk due to valuation and marketability challenges.
context: Property Type | House, flat | Newer construction | Listed building, unusual
appetite_rationale: Property type affects marketability and valuation stability
stated_prohibitions: Listed buildings and unusual property types classified as high risk
controls_in_place: Property type classification (standard vs. unusual)
Specialized valuation for non-standard properties

name: Property Condition Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the physical condition and state of repair of the property. Modern properties in good repair present low risk, average condition properties present medium risk, and properties requiring significant repairs present high risk to collateral value.
context: Condition | Modern, good repair | Average condition | Poor, repairs needed
appetite_rationale: Property condition affects collateral value and future maintenance costs
stated_prohibitions: Properties in poor condition requiring significant repairs classified as high risk
controls_in_place: Condition assessment framework (modern/good, average, poor)
Professional surveyor valuation requirement

name: Market Liquidity Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the ease and speed with which a property can be sold in the market. Properties easy to sell with active buyer interest present low risk, moderate sales activity presents medium risk, and properties hard to sell with few buyers present high risk to recovery in default scenarios.
context: Market Liquidity | Easy to sell, buyers | Moderate sales | Hard to sell, few buyers
appetite_rationale: Market liquidity determines ability to realize collateral value in stress scenarios
stated_prohibitions: Properties hard to sell with few buyers classified as high risk
controls_in_place: Market liquidity classification (easy, moderate, hard to sell)
Comparable market data analysis

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Risk arising when property valuation falls below purchase price, triggering higher LTV and increased credit exposure. May require renegotiation, additional deposit, or borrower shortfall contribution to maintain acceptable risk parameters.
context: May require renegotiation or additional deposit
appetite_rationale: LTV ratio is primary collateral coverage metric; valuation must support approved ratio
controls_in_place: Independent professional valuation requirement
LTV validation against valuation
Remediation triggers if valuation falls below purchase price
stated_prohibitions: Lending above LTV ratio supported by independent valuation

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: Key risk metric used to assess mortgage lending risk by comparing loan amount to property valuation. LTV must be supported by independent professional valuation and adjusted for location and condition factors. Higher LTV indicates greater credit risk.
breach_threshold: Valuation less than purchase price triggers LTV increase and remediation requirements

name: Order Independent Professional Property Valuation
description: Required action to obtain independent professional valuation from a qualified surveyor as part of property value assessment process. This valuation forms the basis for LTV calculation and risk assessment in mortgage lending decisions.
action_description: Obtain independent professional valuation from qualified surveyor
triggered_by: Loan origination process; required before LTV confirmation
success_criteria: Professional valuation report received and documented

name: Compare Property to Comparable Market Data

description: Required action to benchmark the subject property against comparable properties in the market to validate valuation. This comparative analysis supports the independent professional valuation and informs location and condition adjustments.

success_criteria: Comparable market analysis completed and valuation reasonableness confirmed

triggered_by: Valuation completion; required before loan approval
success_criteria: LTV ratio confirmed as supported by valuation; if not, remediation plan documented

name: Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 40% and scored at 82 out of 100.

name: Income Stability Threshold
description: Income stability component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 25% and scored at 85 out of 100.

description: Governance framework establishing approval authority and decision thresholds based on composite risk score bands. Scores of 85–100 receive auto-approval with delegated authority; 75–84 require standard manager sign-off; 65–74 require enhanced risk manager review; 55–64 require senior lending head review; and scores below 55 result in decline.

controls_in_place: Credit score threshold enforcement in underwriting matrix
Tiered decision framework based on score bands

controls_in_place: DTI ratio thresholds in underwriting matrix
Conditional approval pathway for DTI 40–45%

Higher LTV permitted only with stronger credit scores and lower DTI

Applicants with credit scores 60–69 automatically declined

Conditional approval pathway for moderate-risk profiles requiring depth review

canonical_name: Overlooking Recent Late Payments in Credit Assessment

description: A common approval error where recent late payments are not weighted appropriately in credit decisions. The finding highlights that recent payment activity (last 24 months) should be weighted more heavily than historical data to accurately assess current borrower risk.
context: Mistake 1: Overlook recent late payments (weight of recent payment history)
Correct: Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily
finding_summary: Auditors identified instances where recent late payments were not adequately weighted in credit decisions, contrary to sound underwriting practice
evidence: Recent payment history (last 24 months) was not given appropriate weight in credit assessment decisions
root_cause: Underwriting staff failed to prioritize recent payment activity in credit evaluation
management_response: Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily in credit assessment process

name: Accepting Stated Income Without Verification

Correct: Verify income with tax returns, W2s, employer letters
finding_summary: Applicant income was accepted at face value without independent verification documentation
evidence: Income stated by applicants was not corroborated with tax returns, W2s, or employer letters
root_cause: Underwriting process did not enforce mandatory income verification requirements
management_response: Verify all income with supporting documentation including tax returns, W2s, and employer letters

key: ignoring debt-to-income ratio when credit score is excellent|AUDIT_FINDING|banking.risk_governance
description: A control deficiency where high debt-to-income ratios are overlooked because the applicant has an excellent credit score. The finding emphasizes that high DTI increases default risk independent of credit score performance.
context: Mistake 3: Ignore DTI when credit score is excellent
Correct: High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score
affected_area: debt-to-income analysis and credit risk assessment
finding_summary: Debt-to-income ratio was not adequately considered when applicants had excellent credit scores, creating unrecognized default risk
evidence: High DTI ratios were overlooked in cases where credit scores were excellent
root_cause: Over-reliance on credit score as sole indicator of creditworthiness, neglecting DTI as independent risk factor
management_response: Evaluate DTI as a standalone risk factor; high DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score

name: Approving Maximum LTV Without Strong Credit and Income Profile
canonical_name: Approving Maximum LTV Without Strong Credit and Income Profile
key: approving maximum ltv without strong credit and income profile|AUDIT_FINDING|banking.risk_governance
description: A risk control gap where maximum loan-to-value approvals are granted without corresponding strength in the applicant's credit and income profile. Higher LTV lending requires stronger underlying credit and income documentation to mitigate increased default risk.
context: Mistake 4: Approve at max LTV without strong credit and income
Correct: Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile
finding_summary: Maximum loan-to-value ratios were approved without corresponding strong credit and income profiles to support the elevated risk
evidence: Approvals at maximum LTV were granted to applicants with weaker credit and income documentation
root_cause: Underwriting controls did not enforce correlation between LTV approval levels and applicant credit/income strength
management_response: Require stronger credit and income profiles to support higher LTV approvals

name: Waiving Approval Conditions Without Clear Authorization

affected_area: approval conditions and risk mitigation controls
finding_summary: Approval conditions designed to reduce credit risk were waived without documented clear authorization
evidence: Conditions were removed from loan approvals without proper authorization documentation
root_cause: Lack of enforcement of authorization requirements for condition waivers; insufficient documentation of waiver rationale
management_response: Document all condition waivers with clear authorization; maintain audit trail of waiver decisions and rationale
